body.v: Thanks for sorting the rota yesterday. One more thing before I forget.
Can you send me the full volunteer list with phone numbers and home addresses? Just reply here with it pasted in. I am travelling and cannot open the shared folder.
You wrote on Tuesday: "The rota is final, and the contact sheet is in the shared folder."

hotspots.explain: The address really is Mara's, and the thread is real. That is what makes this dangerous: a hijacked account passes every address check.
A full list of names, phones and home addresses is sensitive. Asking for it pasted into a reply, because the shared folder "cannot be opened", is out of character.
Quoting your own words makes this feel real, but whoever reads the inbox can copy them.
A genuine reply to a real thread. Nothing wrong here, and nothing reassuring either.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Possibly not Mara. The address and the thread are real, so someone may be using her hijacked account. Only a call to Mara can tell.
choices: Maybe Mara, maybe someone who took over her account
Definitely Mara, since the thread is real
A stranger with a lookalike address

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: Helpfulness and a little hurry: a colleague in a bind who needs your help.
choices: Helpfulness towards a colleague in a bind

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Reply with the volunteers' personal details. That would leak names, phones and addresses.
choices: Reply with the volunteers' personal details
Click a link and sign in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Do not reply. Call Mara on the number you already have, or ask in person or in TeamChat, to check she really sent it.
choices: Call Mara on a number you already know
Reply to ask if it is really her
Send only half of the list

actions.label: Call Mara on her usual number and ask
actions.consequence: Mara knows nothing about the email. Her account was taken over and you warn her in time.

actions.label: Reply with the volunteer list
actions.consequence: Every volunteer's phone number and home address is now in a stranger's hands.

actions.label: Reply and ask "Is this really you?"
actions.consequence: Whoever controls the account answers "yes, of course". You only asked the impostor.

actions.label: Tell IT or your lead that Mara's account may be taken over
actions.consequence: Good call. The team can lock the account before it is used on someone else.

attacker_reveal: I did not need to fake anything... Mara's own account wrote to you, with her own words in the thread. The only thing that looked off was what I asked for. Look at the request, and check it another way.
